name: Environmental Protection Agency
kicker: Federal agency that enforces pollution laws · Created under Nixon in 1970
briefing: In 1969, an oil-soaked river in Cleveland caught fire, drawing national attention to pollution. The next year, about 20 million Americans took part in the first Earth Day, and President Richard Nixon created the Environmental Protection Agency to enforce national rules on clean air and water. Led first by William Ruckelshaus, the EPA soon banned most uses of the pesticide DDT, which Rachel Carson had warned about in her 1962 book _Silent Spring_.
answerHtml: Environmental Protection Agency (or EPA; do not accept “Department of the Interior” or a law it enforces, such as the “Clean Air Act”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: This agency was created not by a new act of Congress but by Reorganization Plan No. 3, which combined offices from the Departments of the Interior, Agriculture, and Health, Education, and Welfare. It opened in December 1970, months after the first Earth Day.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency that Richard Nixon set up to fight pollution.

tossups.p: This agency’s first leader later resigned as deputy attorney general rather than fire Watergate prosecutor Archibald Cox during the “Saturday Night Massacre.” That man, William Ruckelshaus [“RUCK-ulz-howss”], returned to lead this agency again in the 1980s.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency, created in 1970, that enforces the Clean Air Act.

tossups.p: After months of hearings, this agency’s first head overruled a hearing examiner and in 1972 banned most uses of a pesticide that had thinned the eggshells of bald eagles and brown pelicans.
tossups.r: That pesticide, DDT, had been the focus of Rachel Carson’s _Silent Spring_. For 10 points, name this agency created in 1970.

tossups.p: Families were moved out of the Love Canal neighborhood of Niagara Falls, New York, after chemical waste was found buried beneath their homes and a school. In response, Congress passed a 1980 law that set up a “Superfund” for this agency to clean up toxic waste sites.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency that enforces pollution laws and is known by a three-letter abbreviation.

tossups.p: In 1972, Congress overrode Richard Nixon’s veto to pass the Clean Water Act, which this agency enforces. Support for that law had grown after Cleveland’s Cuyahoga [“ky-uh-HOH-guh”] River, covered with oil and waste, caught fire in 1969.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency that Nixon had created to fight pollution.

tossups.p: In a 2007 case brought by Massachusetts against this agency, the Supreme Court ruled 5–4 that carbon dioxide from new cars counts as an air pollutant that this agency has the power to regulate under the Clean Air Act.
tossups.r: Its first leader was William Ruckelshaus. For 10 points, name this federal agency created under Richard Nixon in 1970.

tossups.p: Rules set by this agency led carmakers to add catalytic converters starting with 1975 models, which meant those cars had to use unleaded gasoline. Lead was later banned from gasoline for cars entirely, starting in 1996.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency that enforces the Clean Air Act and was created under Richard Nixon.

tossups.p: In 1992, this agency started the Energy Star program, which labels computers, appliances, and other products that use less energy. Under the Safe Drinking Water Act of 1974, it also sets limits on harmful substances in public tap water.
tossups.r: It also runs the Superfund program for toxic waste sites. For 10 points, name this federal agency created under Richard Nixon.

tossups.p: Under the Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990, which George H. W. Bush signed, this agency began a program that let power plants buy and sell permits to release sulfur dioxide, a cause of acid rain. That “cap-and-trade” system sharply cut sulfur dioxide pollution.
tossups.r: This agency also banned most uses of DDT in 1972. For 10 points, name this federal agency that Richard Nixon created in 1970.

tossups.p: Wisconsin senator Gaylord Nelson organized a nationwide day of teach-ins about pollution on April 22, 1970, which about 20 million Americans joined. In December of that year, this new federal agency opened its doors.
tossups.r: That April day was the first Earth Day. For 10 points, name this agency that Richard Nixon created.

tossups.p: This agency reviews the environmental impact statements that a law signed on January 1, 1970, requires for major federal projects. That law, the National Environmental Policy Act, also created a White House Council on Environmental Quality.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this agency, created later in 1970, that enforces the Clean Air Act and the Clean Water Act.

tossups.p: In 1983, this agency agreed to buy out the entire town of Times Beach, Missouri, after a chemical called dioxin was found in oil that had been sprayed on its dirt roads to keep down dust. The town’s site later became a state park.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this federal agency that runs the Superfund cleanup program and enforces the Clean Air Act.

tossups.p: After a 1984 gas leak at a chemical plant killed thousands of people in Bhopal, India, Congress passed a 1986 law requiring factories to report the toxic chemicals they release. This agency publishes those reports in the Toxics Release Inventory.
tossups.r: It also enforces the Clean Water Act. For 10 points, name this federal agency founded in 1970 under Richard Nixon.

tossups.p: A 1962 book that opens with “A Fable for Tomorrow,” about an imaginary American town where the birds have stopped singing, helped start the movement that led to this agency. Its author, a former government biologist, died two years after it was published.
tossups.r: That book was Rachel Carson’s _Silent Spring_. For 10 points, name this agency created in 1970 to fight pollution.

tossups.p: Less than a month after this agency opened, a 1970 law ordered it to set national air-quality standards for common pollutants such as carbon monoxide and sulfur dioxide. The same law required large cuts in the exhaust from new cars.
tossups.r: That law was the Clean Air Act. For 10 points, name this agency that Richard Nixon created.

clues.t: Created by President Richard Nixon in 1970; it opened that December
The federal agency that enforces national pollution laws like the Clean Air Act and the Clean Water Act
Banned most uses of the pesticide DDT in 1972
Inspired in part by Rachel Carson’s _Silent Spring_ (1962), a book about the dangers of pesticides
First administrator: William Ruckelshaus (1970–1973, and again 1983–1985)
Created the same year as the first Earth Day (April 22, 1970), organized by Senator Gaylord Nelson
Runs the Superfund program (1980), which cleans up toxic waste sites
Love Canal, a Niagara Falls neighborhood built over buried chemical waste, led to the Superfund law
Cleveland’s Cuyahoga River caught fire in 1969, building support for clean water laws
Congress overrode Nixon’s veto to pass the Clean Water Act (1972)
Created by Reorganization Plan No. 3, which combined offices from Interior, Agriculture, and Health, Education, and Welfare
Ruckelshaus later resigned as deputy attorney general in the Saturday Night Massacre (1973)
Ruckelshaus banned DDT after months of hearings, overruling a hearing examiner; DDT had thinned the eggshells of eagles and pelicans
A 2007 case brought by Massachusetts: the Supreme Court ruled 5–4 that it may regulate carbon dioxide from new cars
Its rules brought catalytic converters (1975 models) and unleaded gasoline; leaded gas for cars was banned starting in 1996
Started the Energy Star label for energy-saving products (1992)
1990 Clean Air Act amendments: a cap-and-trade program for sulfur dioxide to fight acid rain
Reviews the environmental impact statements required by the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), signed January 1, 1970
Bought out Times Beach, Missouri (1983), after dioxin was found in oil sprayed on its roads
Publishes the Toxics Release Inventory, created by a 1986 law passed after the Bhopal disaster in India
_Silent Spring_ opens with “A Fable for Tomorrow,” about a town where the birds no longer sing; Carson died in 1964
Sets limits on harmful substances in tap water under the Safe Drinking Water Act (1974)
The Clean Air Act of 1970 ordered it to set national air-quality standards for pollutants like carbon monoxide and sulfur dioxide

trap.title: Agency, not a law
trap.body: Most tossups on this agency name the laws it enforces, like the Clean Air Act, the Clean Water Act, and Superfund, or events that led to it, like the first Earth Day and Rachel Carson’s _Silent Spring_. Those are separate answer lines, so blurting out a law or an event when the question asks for “this agency” loses the tossup. The Department of the Interior, which runs the National Park Service, is a different part of the government.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “this agency” with Richard Nixon, William Ruckelshaus, the DDT ban, or Love Canal wants the Environmental Protection Agency, and “EPA” is fine. “This law” wants the specific act, and “this day” wants Earth Day.
